theme: Corgi portraits in seasonal cottagecore settings

opportunityScanner.category: Bold & Easy adult coloring books in underserved aesthetic sub-niches (cottagecore, dark academia, witchy/pagan, dog-breed-specific)
opportunityScanner.selectionRationale: This candidate has the strongest triangulated live signal of the set: five-plus independent 2026 sources (KDPEasy, KDPBuilder, BookIllustrationAI, Medium case studies, Automateed) all independently converge on 'Bold and Easy' as the dominant coloring-book growth trend, now carrying real commercial validation via a traditional-publisher acquisition of the style's originator, while also giving concrete, countable competition benchmarks (dark academia under 50 titles, cottagecore under 200) that make differentiation measurable rather than guesswork. It beats the guided-journal candidate on differentiation clarity (exact sub-niche title counts vs. journals' vaguer 'audience specificity' advice) and beats children's picture books on production risk (simple bold-line art is fast and cheap to produce well, whereas picture books require commissioned-quality illustration to compete with trade publishers). Poetry and flash fiction were both grounded in search but showed clearly weaker monetization/demand signals this week. Net: strong, currently-accelerating demand plus a documented, narrow competitive gap make this the best balance of opportunity and differentiation to pursue this week.

scout.suggestedAngle: Structure the book as a 4-season journey (Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter) where each corgi is shown in bold, thick-outlined easy scenes doing a signature cottagecore activity per season—e.g., planting tulips in spring, picnicking in a wildflower meadow in summer, harvesting pumpkins in fall, and sipping cocoa by a fireplace in winter—paired with cottage-style props (mason jars, quilts, garden tools, baskets) to create a giftable, thematically bundled product that stands apart from generic single-season or plain 'dog portrait' coloring books.
scout.selectionRationale: This theme wins by stacking two proven demand drivers—dog-breed specificity and cottagecore aesthetics—into one low-competition long-tail keyword ('corgi coloring book' + seasonal cottage themes) rather than competing in the oversaturated generic dog or dark academia/gothic architecture spaces. It's evergreen (four seasonal sub-volumes possible), easy to execute as true bold/easy line art (a corgi + simple cottage/garden background) without the rendering difficulty of architectural interiors or stained glass, and taps a devoted breed fanbase with strong gifting behavior. It offers the best balance of differentiation, feasible production simplicity, and repeatable series potential of all five candidates.
